name: run_status
description: The broadcast now, numbered by revision: every task with its state, live status and branch, and what is open: questions waiting, prompts waiting on the person (a prompt open in a worker's terminal), tasks ready to accept, tasks one of whose workers ended its turn with work still running in the background, even while another of its tabs works (under background; each task's background lists the commands, and the worker wakes on its own when they end, so it is not ready yet; a worker whose turn ended while its subagent works stays working, its task's background naming the subagent by its description), tasks possibly stalled, anything uncertain. A worker whose live reads working? says working but neither its transcript nor its subagents' has grown for two minutes, and no tool call it started is still running (one counts for up to 30 minutes from its start), so the flag may be stuck: it is listed under uncertain, so look at the worker before trusting it. A task whose first worker was launched a moment ago and has not named its conversation yet says opening: it is still starting and counts as at work, whatever its live says (Codex reads idle for about half a minute). A task whose worker the person is driving, by a prompt they typed into its window themselves, says youAreDriving with yourPrompt, its first line, until that turn ends: leave that worker alone meanwhile, and read its result afterwards as you would one of your own. A task one of whose workers stopped short of finishing on an API error says why under stoppedOn, and is neither ready nor finished without a commit: its usage limit, with when it resets (Claude Code may carry on by itself then, so wait or move the work elsewhere), or a billing or sign-in failure, which won't clear by itself: tell the person. Each task keeps model, the one it was planned on; a Claude worker adds liveModel and liveReasoning, the model and effort Claude Code says it runs now, which change once a /model or /effort has run, never on delivery. A slash command you sent with message_task is listed under slashCommands with what became of it: delivered (typed, nothing in its transcript yet), queued (Claude Code queued it at seenAt and has taken nothing from its queue since), ran (its transcript recorded it at seenAt, with a local command's output), or unknown: nothing of it in its transcript within a minute, or no transcript to read; something left the queue after it was queued; or an hour passed without its run. Within that hour an unknown command can still become ran, as one waiting on a dialog does once the person answers, but not one a remove, popAll or popOne named, nor one never queued once you sent the same text again. A /model or /effort run mid-turn takes effect without a record, so it reads unknown: check liveModel and liveReasoning. A task with tabs added by open_tab lists every worker tab under tabs, its first worker as main, and is ready to accept only once every tab ended its turn; a prompt in an added tab is named task/tab, and a tab that was closed is marked closed and never opened again. Under run it also shows the off-brief finds, the snags you recorded with report_snag (so you don't record one twice after a restart), each agent's weekly use, and under agents each installed agent's models with its default model and, under delivery, whether its workers can be messaged. A task with a merge request shows what the host says of it under mergeRequest (draft, pipeline, mergeable, approvedBy, head), or why it could not be read under mergeRequestNote. A broadcast set up with the Agents, Task and Done steps also shows under run: agents.allowed, its Agents rows (agent, model, reasoning), the only combinations it may start workers, tabs and reviewers on; taskSettings, what every task follows (review, the review prompt; end; closeWhenDone and deleteMergedBranch, its closing at the broadcast's end); goal, with its text and extraRounds; goalCheckDue, true once every task is done and the goal is still to check with check_goal; and roundsUsed. Each task lists reviewVerdicts, the verdicts record_review kept, and finished lists the tasks closed and removed at the broadcast's end, as their records keep them. Call it first after any restart or compaction.

name: jira_search
description: Searches Jira, read-only, within the Jira projects linked to the broadcast's projects.

name: jira_create
description: Creates a Jira ticket in one of the broadcast's Jira projects. Refused unless the broadcast's Jira slice is on, and outside its Jira projects; AiTerm then leaves it for the person. The same key returns the ticket the first call made, so call again with it after a lost reply.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

project.description: The Jira project's key, one of the broadcast's.

type.description: The issue type, such as Task, Bug or Story.

description.description: What the ticket says, in plain text.

parent.description: The key of the epic or parent ticket it belongs under, if any.

name: jira_move
description: Moves a Jira ticket to the status of that name, by the transition that leads there. Refused unless the broadcast's Jira slice is on, and outside its Jira projects. A status the ticket cannot reach from where it is is refused with the statuses it can reach.

key.description: The ticket's key, such as PAY-231.

status.description: The status to move it to, such as In Review or Done.

name: jira_link
description: Links two Jira tickets, read from the first: the first blocks, relates to or duplicates the second. Refused unless the broadcast's Jira slice is on, and when either is outside its Jira projects.

key.description: The ticket the link is read from.

type.description: The Jira link type's name, such as Blocks, Relates or Duplicate.

name: jira_board
description: Reads the Jira boards of each of the broadcast's Jira projects: for each board its id, name and type, its active and future sprints (id, name, state, dates; only a scrum board has any) and its columns with the statuses in each. Read-only; needs no slice. Use a sprint's id with jira_sprint, and a column's status names with jira_move.

name: jira_sprint
description: Puts Jira tickets in an active or future sprint, or back on the backlog. The tickets must be in the broadcast's Jira projects, and a sprint must be on one of their boards (jira_board lists them). Refused unless the broadcast's Jira slice is on; AiTerm then leaves it for the person. The same key again moves nothing, so call again with it after a lost reply.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

tickets.description: The tickets' keys, such as PAY-231; at most 50.

sprint.description: The sprint's id from jira_board, or backlog to take the tickets out of their sprints.

name: jira_edit
description: Edits a ticket of one of the broadcast's Jira projects: its summary, description, labels (added and removed, the others stay), priority, fix versions or assignee. Name at least one. Refused unless the broadcast's Jira slice is on, and outside its Jira projects; AiTerm then leaves it for the person. Setting the same values again changes nothing, so call again after a lost reply.

ticket.description: The ticket's key, such as PAY-231.

description.description: The new description, in plain text; it replaces the old one, and an empty one clears it.

priority.description: The priority's name, such as High.

fixVersions.description: The version names the ticket ends with, replacing its fix versions; empty clears them.

assignee.description: me, none, or a name or email that matches exactly one person Jira can assign the ticket to; several matches are refused with their names.

name: jira_comment
description: Comments on a ticket of one of the broadcast's Jira projects. A comment reaches the ticket's watchers, so write it for them. Refused unless the broadcast's Jira slice is on, and outside its Jira projects; AiTerm then leaves it for the person. The same key again posts nothing: after a lost reply call again with it, and AiTerm looks for the comment on the ticket before it posts anything.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

ticket.description: The ticket's key, such as PAY-231.

name: create_task
description: Adds an unstarted task to the open plan revision, in one of the broadcast's projects. The same key in this broadcast returns the task already made. Once the first plan is submitted, additions past a quarter of its size need the Oracle's yes. One the Oracle refuses, or any past that limit with the Oracle off, is refused and noted for the summary by AiTerm.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

title.description: The task's title, as its row shows it.

brief.description: The worker's first prompt: everything it needs, since it sees nothing else.

project.description: The project it belongs to, one of the broadcast's, by name or by id from run_status.

ticket.description: The Jira key it works, if any.

issueType.description: The Jira issue type, or feat, fix or chore. Sets the branch prefix.

agent.description: The agent that works the task, among those installed.

model.description: A model id from the agent's own list, as run_status shows it under agents. Left out, the agent's default. A model not in that list is refused. In a broadcast whose run_status lists rows under agents.allowed, only a row's model, and left out, the agent's first row.

reasoning.description: The model's reasoning level, as Settings › Agents lists it. Explicit reasoning wins. Left out, the configured default model keeps its configured reasoning, even when named explicitly; another model takes its catalogue fallback. In a broadcast with taskSettings, the agent, model and reasoning must be a row under agents.allowed: anything else is refused, naming the rows. Ask the person with ask_you about a combination outside those rows.

modelReason.description: Why this agent and model, in one line, as the task's card and the summary show it.

agentPinned.description: True when the person's words named this task's agent: it then starts on that agent whatever its weekly use.

end.description: Where the task ends, from the broadcast's Done when: commit; draftMR, push and open a draft merge request; merge, push, open a merge request and merge it once the host says it can be; or mergeLocal, merge the accepted commit into the project's own default branch, with nothing pushed. A merge needs the broadcast's Merge slice. Left out, a task ends at a draftMR, or at a commit when the Done says a commit. In a broadcast whose run_status shows taskSettings, every task ends at its end and this is refused with: Every task ends at <end>, which only the person changes.

dependsOn.description: What the task waits for. An order dependency waits until the other task is accepted or needs no change; a code dependency also builds on its accepted commit, in the same project. At most one code dependency.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

challengeId.description: The challengeId a challenged call returned: send it with your revised arguments, or with challengeReply. A reply that says pending has no answer yet: call again with its challengeId and the same arguments. For create_task, finish_task and check_goal, the call again acts only on the Oracle's yes. The same challengeId again, once answered, returns the recorded result.

challengeReply.description: Your answer to each point of the second opinion's critique, when you keep the act as it was.

name: update_task
description: Changes an unstarted task's brief, agent, model, reasoning, end or dependencies. In a broadcast started with the Agents and Task steps, combinations stay within its Agents rows. Steer a started task with message_task instead.

A merge needs the broadcast's Merge slice. Left out, a task ends at a draftMR, or at a commit when the Done says a commit. In a broadcast whose run_status shows taskSettings, every task ends at its end and this is refused with: Every task ends at <end>, which only the person changes.

name: submit_plan
description: Closes a plan revision: its planned tasks are queued at once, with nothing to approve. Submitting the same revision again returns the earlier result.

A reply that says pending has no answer yet: call again with its challengeId and the same arguments. For create_task, finish_task and check_goal, the call again acts only on the Oracle's yes. The same challengeId again, once answered, returns the recorded result.

name: read_task
description: Reads a task: its worker's last message, its diff, the prompt open in its session, or its review: the agent review's findings, and for a task whose request people review, its threads with their ids, who approved and who was asked. A task with tabs added by open_tab: tab names the one whose last message or prompt to read. A key the task has no tab for is refused with its tabs.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

tab.description: For lastMessage and prompt, the key of the tab to read, as run_status lists it. Left out, or main, the first worker.

name: review_task
description: Starts an agent review of a working task's branch, or its accepted commit while inReview: another agent reads its commits, diff and worktree headless and read-only, as instructions asks, a skill they name passed to it as text. The reviewer reads files only: it runs no commands and dispatches no subagents, so it can't run git or a skill's subagent, and says on its first line which steps of a named skill it skipped. When the person's Review requires a skill's exact workflow and that needs commands or subagents, run it in a worker tab instead: open_tab with a read-only brief. That tab's review is not recorded as this task's agent review. Nobody is notified, so it needs no slice. It answers started at once; AiTerm wakes you when the findings are in, and read_task with what: review reads them. Have the task's agent fix them with message_task. A review running already, or the same review of the same commit, is not started again. In a broadcast whose run_status shows taskSettings it is refused with: Run the review in a tab: open_tab with role review, then record_review.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

instructions.description: What the review checks and how, from the broadcast's Review, such as an adversarial review with /review-skill.

agent.description: Who reviews: claude, codex or pi. Left out, the other of Claude and Codex from the task's own agent.

name: request_review
description: Marks a task's merge request ready and asks people to review it. Refused unless the broadcast's Review slice is on; AiTerm then leaves it for the person. The same reviewers again change nothing.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

reviewers.description: The usernames to ask, as find_user gives them.

name: reply_thread
description: Replies in a review thread on a task's merge request, by the thread's id from read_task with what: review. Refused unless the broadcast's Review slice is on. The same key posts once.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

name: find_user
description: Finds people on the code host of a task's project who may review there, by username or name. It only reads, so it needs no slice.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

query.description: A username or a name, or part of one.

name: message_task
description: Sends a started task's worker a message, typed into its session by AiTerm's rules. Returns delivered, partial (pasted, its Enter held back) or refused, with the reason; nothing is retried. Delivered is typed and entered, not run: what became of a slash command sent to a Claude worker shows in run_status, under its task's slashCommands for the first worker and under that tab's tabs[].slashCommands for a tab added by open_tab. Claude Code saves a /model or /effort that runs as the person's default for new sessions. A task with tabs added by open_tab: tab names the one to message. A key the task has no tab for is refused with its tabs. Messaging an accepted task that isn't published yet sends it back to working; accept its new commit again.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

tab.description: The key of the tab to message, as run_status lists it. Left out, or main, the first worker.

name: open_tab
description: Adds a worker tab to a task that is working or in review: another agent in the task's window, on the same worktree and branch, for more work on that task. It is part of the task: one card, one branch, accepted once. Its first prompt is your brief, after AiTerm's lines on where it works and that it shares the worktree. It opens behind the person's work. The same key on the same task returns the first call's tab and opens nothing more; the same key with other arguments is refused. Returns the tab's key, agent, model, and opened or opening.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

agent.description: The agent that works the task, among those installed.

model.description: A model id from the agent's own list, as run_status shows it under agents. Left out, the agent's default. A model not in that list is refused. In a broadcast whose run_status lists rows under agents.allowed, only a row's model, and left out, the agent's first row.

reasoning.description: The model's reasoning level, as Settings › Agents lists it. Explicit reasoning wins. Left out, the configured default model keeps its configured reasoning, even when named explicitly; another model takes its catalogue fallback. In a broadcast with taskSettings, the agent, model and reasoning must be a row under agents.allowed: anything else is refused, naming the rows. Ask the person with ask_you about a combination outside those rows.

modelReason.description: Why this agent and model, in one line.

agentPinned.description: True when the person's words named this agent: an agent whose workers can't be messaged is then not refused.

brief.description: The tab's first prompt: what this worker does, since it sees nothing else. Needed for a work tab, and for every tab of a broadcast started before the Agents and Task steps; optional for a review tab, whose first prompt is the broadcast's review prompt with AiTerm's lines, and what you write is added after it.

role.description: Only in a broadcast started with the Agents and Task steps, whose run_status shows taskSettings; a broadcast started before them doesn't take it. work, more work on the task; or review, a reviewer of the task's branch head as the tab opens, which only reviews and ends with a verdict: read it once its turn ends and call record_review. Run each review this way, on a row of agents.allowed, another agent than the task's worker where the rows have one. Left out, work.

name: record_review
description: Records a review tab's verdict on a task, once its turn ended and you read it: the commit it reviewed, whether it passed by the review prompt's own words, its findings counted, and its fix round. sha must be on the task's branch and tab one of its review tabs (open_tab with role review). The same key returns the first answer. It answers the task's verdicts and how many failed. You decide when to accept: AiTerm doesn't refuse an acceptance without a passing verdict. When the rounds the prompt names are used up, ask the person with ask_you on the task, about fixRounds.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

sha.description: The commit it reviewed, as its first prompt named it.

passed.description: Whether it passed, by the review prompt's own words.

critical.description: How many critical findings it reported.

important.description: How many important findings it reported.

minor.description: How many minor findings it reported.

round.description: The fix round this review closes, counted by you from 1.

rounds.description: The rounds of fixes the review prompt allows, when it names a number.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

name: check_goal
description: Answers the broadcast's goal once every task is done: refused unless run_status shows goalCheckDue, when AiTerm wakes you for it. Say whether the goal is met, with evidence from each task's result, and when not, what is still missing, one line each. With the Oracle on it needs the Oracle's yes that your verdict is right; without its answer it acts unchallenged. It answers complete, the broadcast done and its summary asked for; planMore, with the rounds left: plan only what missing names (create_task, then submit_plan), and if nothing can be planned call check_goal again before submitting anything; or stopped, with what went to leftForYou: not met with no rounds left, or not met again when nothing could be planned after planMore, rounds left or not.

evidence.description: Why, from each task's result: its accepted commit, its merge and its verdicts.

missing.description: When not met: what is still to do, one line each.

challengeId.description: The challengeId a challenged call returned: send it with your revised arguments, or with challengeReply. A reply that says pending has no answer yet: call again with its challengeId and the same arguments. For create_task, finish_task and check_goal, the call again acts only on the Oracle's yes. The same challengeId again, once answered, returns the recorded result.

challengeReply.description: Your answer to each point of the second opinion's critique, when you keep the act as it was.

name: mark_task
description: Records a working task's outcome: accepted, with the result commit on its branch and the worker's check output; noChange; blocked or failed, with the reason in note. Identical evidence for the same commit returns the earlier result. Fresh checkOutput or note refreshes evidence only after verifying the same current branch head, and invalidates the previous merge verdict. After an obsolete merge refusal, refresh with mark_task then start a fresh finish_task call. run_status exposes acceptanceEvidence with commit, output and time.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

sha.description: The accepted commit, unmoved on the task's branch.

checkOutput.description: The worker's check output: tests, lint, build.

challengeId.description: The challengeId a challenged call returned: send it with your revised arguments, or with challengeReply. A reply that says pending has no answer yet: call again with its challengeId and the same arguments. For create_task, finish_task and check_goal, the call again acts only on the Oracle's yes. The same challengeId again, once answered, returns the recorded result.

challengeReply.description: Your answer to each point of the second opinion's critique, when you keep the act as it was.

name: resume_task
description: Puts a blocked task back to work once its reason is resolved; the same worker session continues. AiTerm blocks after 90 minutes of work without a new task-branch commit or 4 hours of total work since starting or the last resume. Any worker tab's commit resets only the no-commit clock. A task ready for acceptance is never blocked on runtime. Inspect before resuming; resume_task resets both clocks.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

name: retry_task
description: Queues a failed task again, if it has retries left.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

name: finish_task
description: Carries out an accepted task's end from the plan, for its accepted commit only. draft MR: pushes the task's own branch and opens a draft merge request; a stacked task's targets its parent's branch, so finish the parent first. merge: pushes, opens a merge request and merges it at the accepted commit, once the host calls it mergeable with its pipelines green, read twice at least 30 seconds apart. A stacked task waits for its parent's merge, then retargets to the default branch. While it waits this answers waitingToMerge, and AiTerm wakes you when it merged or is blocked; after about an hour of waiting it answers blocked. A failed pipeline or a conflict blocks it: have the worker fix it, accept the new commit, and call finish_task again. A task that ends in a commit has nothing to finish. The task goes into review instead when the Review slice is on and its review is written: the broadcast's Review, or, in a broadcast started with the Agents and Task steps, the task's review prompt. Its request then opens as a draft and this answers inReview: AiTerm wakes you on people's feedback, and the next finish_task after the last fix ends the review, a draft end published, a merge end going on to merge. A merge, through the request or local, is refused unless the broadcast's Merge slice is on; AiTerm then leaves it for the person. Before it merges a request that is still a draft, AiTerm marks it ready, only to merge it, and it merges only with every one of its review threads resolved. mergeLocal: merges the accepted commit into the project's own checkout's default branch and never pushes; that checkout must be on its default branch with nothing uncommitted. AiTerm leaves the push for the person, as "Push main in <project>: merged locally." A merge or mergeLocal end whose accepted commit is already in its default branch, merged outside finish_task by the person or a worker, is recorded as merged: nothing is pushed or merged, AiTerm never writes to the host, and the Oracle isn't asked, so call finish_task for such work, even after a refused merge or one left for the person. AiTerm leaves pushing a default branch that has it only locally, and closing a request still open from the task's branch, for the person. With the Oracle on, a finish_task that would merge first needs the Oracle's yes that the merge conditions hold: those written in the broadcast's Review and Done, or, in a broadcast started with the Agents and Task steps, the task's review prompt, its verdicts and the person's answers to its fix-rounds questions; a no is recorded on the task and refuses the merge. A push the repository's pre-push hook refused fails with the hook's output as its reason. noVerify pushes past the hook, and only after such a refusal; with the Oracle on it first needs the Oracle's yes that the hook failed on the environment, not the code, judged from that output and your reason. A call that also merges asks both at once, and only a yes to both acts. It answers result: published, inReview, waitingToMerge, blocked, refused or failed, with reason, mergeRequest, pushedSHA, merged and mergedSHA as far as they are known; refused and failed also say what was already done. draftNote says what this call did to the request's draft state (opened as a draft, opened ready, left as a draft, marked ready), and is left out when it did nothing. Each step is recorded and calling again resumes at the next step: it never pushes or opens a request twice, and on a task that is done it answers what was done. A push that timed out may have landed: call finish_task again. A takeover stops a merge's waiting: call finish_task again once the task is handed back. Refused if the task ends in a commit, the task was taken over, its branch moved past the accepted commit (unless that commit is already in the default branch), its parent was accepted again, the broadcast is paused, stopped or offline, the host protects its branch or cannot say whether it does, or it is the default branch. AiTerm never deploys, never force-pushes, and never pushes to a default or protected branch.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

noVerify.description: Skip the repository's push hooks: only when the hook failed on the environment and your repair didn't work. The Oracle judges it.

reason.description: With noVerify: what you tried to repair the environment, for the Oracle. Left out, it reads your last shell commands in the task's worktree.

challengeId.description: The challengeId a challenged call returned: send it with your revised arguments, or with challengeReply. A reply that says pending has no answer yet: call again with its challengeId and the same arguments. For create_task, finish_task and check_goal, the call again acts only on the Oracle's yes. The same challengeId again, once answered, returns the recorded result.

challengeReply.description: Your answer to each point of the second opinion's critique, when you keep the act as it was.

name: ask_you
description: Lists a question you asked in your chat under Waiting on you, with the same text, and notifies the person. They answer in this window; close it with resolve_question. The same key returns the open question.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

question.description: The question, complete on its own.

task.description: When its worker is itself stopped on the answer or when its fix rounds are used up (about: fixRounds): the task, by its key or its id from run_status. Your row then shows waiting on the person, naming the task, and the task waits for the answer: it isn't ready to accept and isn't watched for stalls until you resolve the question. Other questions about your own next step, such as a reviewer's username, a scope choice or a merge decision, go on no task.

about.description: What the question is about, when its task's card answers it: fixRounds, a task whose review used up its fix rounds, asked on that task. Its card then offers One More Round and Accept As It Is. Left out for any other question.

name: resolve_question
description: Closes a question: answered by the person, or withdrawn by you when it became moot. Record the answer in summary for a question you asked with ask_you, or AiTerm's question about a merge on the host, which only the person decides. Call it at once when they answer in your chat. A worker's prompt is refused: AiTerm closes it itself once the worker leaves the prompt. A gate- question, opened when your shell's command needs the person's word, is answered with allow true or false, from what the person said in this chat. If your own question or a gate- command became moot, set withdrawn true with a one-line reason in summary, and tell the person you withdrew it and why. Withdrawal grants nothing; allow true must be left out. Host-merge questions cannot be withdrawn. An already resolved question returns its recorded outcome unchanged; answeredInWindow must be checked and resolved as an answer, not withdrawn.

summary.description: The answer or withdrawal reason, in one line.

withdrawn.description: Withdraw your own moot question or gate command, without granting permission.

allow.description: For a gate- question only: whether the person allowed the command.

name: report_find
description: Records something off-brief that you or an agent found, such as a leak in another module: it is not worked on, and the summary may mention it with why it matters. With the broadcast's Jira slice on, AiTerm also files it as a Task in the first of its Jira projects and answers the ticket's key, or why it could not. The same key is recorded once.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

title.description: The find, in a few words.

why.description: Why it matters, in one line.

name: report_snag
description: Records that AiTerm itself showed you something wrong and you worked around it: a state that was not true, a prompt it missed, a tab it lost. After you checked the real source (the tab, git, the host), say what AiTerm showed, what was true, and how you got unstuck. AiTerm keeps it beside the summary, and the person can start an AiTerm task from it to fix the bug. A find (report_find) is about the project's code; a snag is about AiTerm itself. It needs no slice, and nothing is filed or sent. The same key is recorded once.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

title.description: The snag, in a few words.

showed.description: What AiTerm showed, such as a status or a count, in one sentence.

actual.description: What was true, and how you checked it, in one sentence.

workaround.description: What you did to carry on, in one sentence.

evidence.description: Optional: the exact text, state or output that shows it, such as a line from the tab.

task.description: The task it happened on, by its key or its id from run_status. Left out when it is not about a task.

name: leave_for_you
description: Records what a slice kept you from doing, naming what is left and why. It changes no task and sends nothing. The same key is recorded once.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

text.description: What is left for the person and why, in one sentence.

name: log_decision
description: Writes a decision you took on your own to the broadcast's log, for the summary. The same key is written once.

key.description: Your idempotency key for this act: the same key again returns what the first call did.

text.description: The decision, in a few words.

task.description: The task: its key as you gave it to create_task, or its id from run_status.

why.description: Why you decided it, in one sentence.

objection.description: The Oracle's objection, when you decided against it.

name: write_summary
description: When the broadcast is complete, write its summary with write_summary: a few short paragraphs, in plain prose, no lists or headings. Say what was done and how it went, honestly: what went wrong and how it was handled, not only what succeeded. Fold in what you decided on your own and what you found along the way. Keep it short enough to read in a minute. Refused until the broadcast is complete; calling it again replaces the summary.

text.description: The summary: a few short paragraphs of plain prose.
